title: feat(scenarios): run-scenarios --driver codex and --driver external:COMMAND, with the driver on each gallery app page
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XSm2B8fDTCJGABZvwCSJJvu)_

Fixes #31159

Clause-②: yes
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:场景执行器新增两种驱动。`--driver codex` 用本机 Codex CLI(`codex exec --json`)跑卡片,只认 ChatGPT 套餐登录;`--driver external:命令` 让任何能按约定读写 JSON 的命令接进来(每次调用一个进程,stdin 进 JSON、stdout 出 JSON,约定写在包 README)。画廊每个应用页多一行 `- Driver:`,写明驱动名和版本;回放记录写明原录制的驱动。
- 为什么改:维护者原话「前面的建议都同意，立卡」(epic cloud#3600):同一张卡要能横向比较不同 agent 工具。WorkBuddy 只做核查:没找到无头模式加结构化输出的入口,所以不接,也不做 UI 桥。
- 风险与回滚:只动 `packages/qa/scenarios`,默认驱动 `claude` 的行为不变(只是把进程启动函数挪到 `drivers/process.ts` 共用)。最大的风险是人物 API key 泄露:key 只写进 0600 文件(外部命令拿到的是文件路径;Codex 是 `$CODEX_HOME` 下的临时 profile),用完即删,从不进 argv、环境变量或 stdin;端到端测试把整张 crm 卡经外部命令跑完,再在运行记录、录制、评分卡和画廊导出里逐文件搜 key。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/drivers/external.ts`(外部约定与 key 文件)、`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/drivers/codex.ts`(登录守卫、profile 文件、JSONL 解析)、`packages/qa/scenarios/test/runner/external-driver.test.ts`(端到端 key 搜索)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter '@objectstack/scenarios^...' build && pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios exec vitest run test/runner/external-driver.test.ts test/runner/codex-driver.test.ts`,预期 2 个文件 20/20 通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- **`--driver external:COMMAND`** (`src/runner/drivers/external.ts`, `ExternalDriver`): the `AgentDriver` seam as a process contract, `objectstack-scenario-driver/1`.
  - One process per call. The call is one JSON object on stdin, the answer one JSON object on stdout, logs on stderr (the record keeps the last 2,000 characters). Three calls: `info` once at start (the command names itself and its version: the record's driver is `external:NAME`, its version the one it gives; a command that cannot answer is refused before any card runs), `author` (`step`, `prompt`, `cwd`, `tier`, `limits`; runs in `cwd`) and `ask` (`step`, `prompt`, `mcp: { url, configFile }`, `limits`; runs in the config file's directory).
  - The answer is strict (`ExternalTurnSchema`: `replyText`, `toolCalls[{name, input, output, isError}]`, optional `model` and `numTurns`; an unknown key is refused). Exit 0 with that shape is the turn. A non-zero exit, a signal or the runner's timeout is a failed turn `no-result(exit N)`; stdout that is not one JSON object of that shape is `invalid-output(…)` with `isError`. A failed authoring turn leaves its Build half not measured (`authorNotMeasured`), a failed persona turn is graded on its empty reply. Never an empty pass.
  - ⛔ The key: `ask` writes `{"mcpServers":{"app":{"type":"http","url":…,"headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer KEY"}}}}` (the Claude driver's `--mcp-config` shape) to a 0600 file in a fresh temp directory, passes its PATH in `mcp.configFile`, and deletes the directory when the call returns. The key is never on argv, in the environment or on stdin.
  - `limits` carries `timeoutMs` (`--author-timeout` for `author`, 5 min for `ask`; the runner kills the call then) and, when given, `maxTurns` and `model`. The command may ignore them; the record states them (`DriverInfo`, `meta.process.maxTurns` / `requestedModel`).
  - The command is split on whitespace (no shell); a word starting `./` or `../`, and a first word holding `/`, resolves against the directory the runner starts in. The runner removes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `CODEX_API_KEY` from the command's environment; it cannot see the command's login, so `authMethod` reads `not verified (an external command: …)`.
- **`--driver codex`** (`src/runner/drivers/codex.ts`, `CodexDriver`), built from the installed CLI (measurements below):
  - Login: refuses to start while `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `CODEX_API_KEY` is set, or when `codex login status` says anything but `Logged in using ChatGPT` (`assertCodexSubscriptionLogin`, pure, the counterpart of `assertSubscriptionLogin`); every turn also passes `-c forced_login_method="chatgpt"`, and both variables are removed from every child.
  - A turn: `codex exec --json --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check -c forced_login_method="chatgpt" -c approval_policy="never" -p PROFILE -s … -C DIR [-m MODEL] -`, the prompt on stdin. Authoring: `-s workspace-write -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true` in the project (the Claude driver's Bash has the network too). Persona turns: `-s read-only` in an empty temp directory.
  - MCP and the key: a profile layer `$CODEX_HOME/scenario-runner-HEX16.config.toml`, mode 0600, deleted in `finally`, holding `[mcp_servers."app"]` with `url` and `http_headers = { Authorization = "Bearer …" }`, plus `enabled = false` for every server of the user's own config (`codex mcp list --json`, read once at start), the counterpart of `--strict-mcp-config`. argv carries the profile's NAME only. A user server already named `app` is refused at start.
  - `parseCodexJsonl` reads the events into the same `ParsedTurn`: `agent_message` texts joined into `replyText`; `mcp_tool_call` → the app's own tool name (`rawName` `mcp__SERVER__TOOL`), output the result's text (or `structured_content`, or the error message), `isError` on `failed`; `command_execution`, `file_change`, `web_search` kept as calls by their item type; a call started and never completed keeps `output: undefined`; `turn.completed` → `success`; `turn.failed` → `turn.failed: MESSAGE` with `isError`; a top-level `error` event is a reconnect notice, not the end.
  - Flags: `--model`, `--author-model`, `--ask-model` → `-m` per turn kind; `--author-timeout` is the runner's own clock. `codex exec` has no turn cap, so `--author-max-turns` and `--ask-max-turns` are refused at `makeDriver` (as the recorded driver refuses every live flag).
- **The driver on record** (Ask 4): `DriverInfo` gains `replayOf?: { driver, version? }`, which `RecordedDriver.info()` fills from the recording (a recording of a replay keeps the original). The gallery exporter writes `- Driver: NAME VERSION` on every app page (`driverText`, exported from `./export`); a replay reads `RECORDED-DRIVER VERSION (re-graded from a recording of that run)`, never the recording's path; an old replay record with no `replayOf` says it does not name its driver. The record schema reads `env.driver.version` / `replayOf` (loose, both optional).
- **Shared process runner**: `runCli` and `noResult` moved from `driver.ts` to `src/runner/drivers/process.ts` (`runTurnProcess`, now taking the child environment), unchanged otherwise; the tool-result text reader moved there too (`contentText`) and `transcript.ts` uses it. `process.ts` is not re-exported from `./runner`.
- `makeDriver`: `codex` and `external:COMMAND` (an empty command refused); the unknown-driver message lists `claude, codex, external:COMMAND, recorded:FILE`. `ApiBillingRefusedError` takes an optional `{ tool, login }` (default Claude Code's, message unchanged).
- README: the Codex section and the external contract (stdin shapes for `info`/`author`/`ask`, the stdout shape, exit codes, timeout, limits, the key file), and the WorkBuddy finding. Changeset `patch` with both declaration lines.

### Public surface (Clause-②: yes, additive)

Nothing removed or renamed. Added to `@objectstack/scenarios/runner`: `CodexDriver`, `CodexDriverOptions`, `CODEX_API_BILLING_ENV`, `CODEX_TURN_CONFIG`, `CODEX_APP_SERVER`, `codexSubscriptionOnlyEnv`, `assertCodexSubscriptionLogin`, `codexProfileToml`, `parseCodexJsonl`, `ExternalDriver`, `ExternalDriverOptions`, `EXTERNAL_DRIVER_CONTRACT`, `EXTERNAL_STRIPPED_ENV`, `ExternalLimits`, `ExternalInfoInput`, `ExternalAuthorInput`, `ExternalAskInput`, `ExternalInfoSchema`, `ExternalToolCallSchema`, `ExternalTurnSchema`, `ExternalTurn`, `parseExternalCommand`; the optional member `DriverInfo.replayOf`; an optional second parameter on `ApiBillingRefusedError`. Added to `./export`: `driverText`. CLI: `--driver codex`, `--driver external:COMMAND`.

### Ask 2: what was measured on the Codex CLI

Installed `@openai/codex@0.167.0` (npm, `codex-cli 0.167.0`, linux-x64) into a scratch prefix in this container. No model turn ran: no login was used, and the container's proxy refuses OpenAI's hosts (`HTTP CONNECT failed with status 403`), so every `exec` below stopped at the model call.

<details><summary>Readings, each with its source</summary>

- `codex --help`, `codex exec --help` (installed binary): `exec` "Run Codex non-interactively"; `[PROMPT]` "If not provided as an argument (or if `-` is used), instructions are read from stdin"; `--json` "Print events to stdout as JSONL"; `-m, --model`; `-s, --sandbox read-only|workspace-write|danger-full-access`; `-C, --cd`; `--skip-git-repo-check`; `--ephemeral` "Run without persisting session files to disk"; `-p, --profile` "Layer $CODEX_HOME/NAME.config.toml on top of the base user config"; `--ignore-user-config`; `-c key=value`; `--strict-config`. No turn-cap flag; `max_turns` and its spellings appear nowhere in the binary's strings.
- JSONL event shapes: `codex-rs/exec/src/exec_events.rs` at tag `rust-v0.167.0` (raw.githubusercontent.com): `thread.started {thread_id}`, `turn.started`, `turn.completed {usage}`, `turn.failed {error{message}}`, `item.started|updated|completed {item{id,type,…}}`, `error {message}`; item types `agent_message {text}`, `mcp_tool_call {server, tool, arguments, result{content, structured_content}, error{message}, status}`, `command_execution {command, aggregated_output, exit_code, status}`, `file_change`, `web_search`, `todo_list`, `reasoning`, `error`. No event carries the served model. Seen live: `thread.started`, `turn.started`, then `error` events `Reconnecting... 2/5 (…)` while the turn continued, so a top-level `error` is read as a notice. The docs the repository ships (`docs/exec.md`, `docs/config.md`, `docs/authentication.md` at that tag) only point to developers.openai.com, which this container cannot reach (connect refused): the config reference was not read; every config key below was measured instead.
- MCP from a profile: `$CODEX_HOME/scen.config.toml` with `[mcp_servers.app] url = "http://127.0.0.1:39123/mcp"`, `http_headers = { Authorization = "Bearer FAKEKEY123" }`: `codex -p scen mcp list --json` shows it `streamable_http` with that header; `codex exec --json -p scen …` POSTed `initialize` to a local listener with `authorization: Bearer FAKEKEY123` (`clientInfo.name` `codex-mcp-client`). A project `.codex/config.toml` in the working directory was not read by `mcp list` (untrusted directory), so the driver does not use one.
- The user's servers: with a base `config.toml` server `other` (port 39124) and the profile's `app` (39123), plain `exec -p scen` contacted both; `--ignore-user-config -p scen` contacted neither (it drops the profile too); `[mcp_servers.other] enabled = false` in the profile → `mcp list` shows it `enabled: false`, and `exec` contacted `app` only. The key appeared in no file under `$CODEX_HOME` but the profile.
- Login: `codex login --with-api-key` (a fake key) → `codex login status` prints on stderr `API key configured - sk-fake-***-0000`, exit 0; an empty `CODEX_HOME` → `Not logged in`, exit 1, also with `CODEX_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` set; the binary's strings hold `Logged in using ChatGPT` (and `… using access token`, `… personal access token`, `… workload identity`, `… Amazon Bedrock …`). With `-c forced_login_method="chatgpt"`, the API-key login reads `Not logged in`, exit 1.
- Config keys under `exec --strict-config -c …`: `forced_login_method="chatgpt"`, `approval_policy="never"` and `sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true` are accepted; `forced_login_method="bogus"` → "expected `chatgpt` or `api`", `approval_policy="bogus"` → "expected one of `untrusted`, `on-failure`, `on-request`, `granular`, `never`", `sandbox_workspace_write.bogus_key` and `bogus_top` → "unknown configuration field".
- Not measured: a real `codex exec` turn end to end (no ChatGPT login here, and live model runs are paused by the maintainer, cloud#3600), so a `turn.completed` stream was not seen live; its shape is the source's. The stand-in in `codex-driver.test.ts` replays those shapes.

</details>

### Ask 3: WorkBuddy

Checked on 2026-11-07; no wiring, no UI bridge.

- npm search `workbuddy`: the one package calling itself a WorkBuddy command line, `@workbuddy/cli-vnext@1.0.153` (maintainer `workbuddy_developer`, `developer@workbuddy.com`), read from its tarball without running it: a REST client for a WorkBuddy tenant API (`commander`; commands `auth`, `profiles`, `use`, `whoami`; options `--base-url`, `--client-id`, `--output json|table|raw`), with no agent, no prompt mode and no MCP client. Its only URL is `https://yourcompany.workbuddy.com`; it is not Tencent's WorkBuddy.
- Tencent's WorkBuddy (CN and the international WorkBuddy AI) is a desktop app: the community `dsh-workbuddy-provider` README (npm) describes reusing "WorkBuddy 桌面 App" credentials on macOS, and the app's model catalogue is fetched with "内置 CLI 版本号" (a built-in CLI version), but no published, documented headless mode with structured output and an MCP client was found.
- So the PR says no, per the card. If one appears, it is a wrapper on `--driver external:` (README), not runner code.

## Tests

- **`test/runner/external-driver.test.ts`** (new, 8 cases), against `test/runner/fixtures/fake-external-driver.mjs`, a stand-in command that speaks the contract and reports what it saw of the key (a SHA-256, never the key):
  - `info` names the driver and version; a command exiting 4, printing prose, or missing is refused at construction with the reason.
  - `author`: the exact stdin object, the call running in the project, the answer read into the turn (MCP prefix dropped, `isError` kept, `model`, `numTurns`, `success`), the project files snapshotted.
  - `ask`: the config file is 0600, holds the URL and the key, the call runs in its directory, the key is on neither argv, environment nor stdin, and the file and its directory are gone afterwards.
  - Failed calls: exit 3 → `no-result(exit 3)` and not measured; prose → `invalid-output(stdout is not one JSON object)`; another shape → `invalid-output(…)` (is_error); a hang → killed at the timeout, `author timed out after 0.03 min`.
  - Command parsing, `external:` with no command refused, the unknown-driver list; every flag in `limits` and on the record.
  - **End to end, the key pin**: the real `crm_account_with_contacts` card through `runCard` (both modes), each scripted turn sent through the stand-in command (the exporter fixture's in-memory app; `runCrm` gains `keyPrefix` and `wrap`), every persona and the admin issued a key `sk-scenario-e2e-key-9f27c1d4` + the persona id. Every ask read one of those keys from a 0600 file and from nowhere else, and each file is gone. Then the run record (where the CLI writes it), the recording, the scorecard (`renderScorecard`) and the full gallery export (`exportGallery`, which exported the card) are written, and every written file is searched for the key prefix: none holds it. The record names `external:fake-agent 1.2.3`, the app page reads `- Driver: external:fake-agent 1.2.3`; a replay of that recording names `replayOf` and its page reads `(re-graded from a recording of that run)` without the recording's path.
- **`test/runner/codex-driver.test.ts`** (new, 12 cases), against a stand-in `codex` script (it answers `--version`, `login status` on stderr, `mcp list --json`, and for `exec` reads the profile it is pointed at):
  - `parseCodexJsonl` on the 0.167.0 shapes (pairing, failed MCP call, command execution, a call cut short, torn last line, notice not an end, `turn.failed`).
  - The cost guard: `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `CODEX_API_KEY` set, an API-key login, no login, an empty status, a non-plan login (its masked credential not echoed) refused; the billing variables stripped.
  - `codexProfileToml` exact text (TOML-escaped key and names).
  - The driver: version and login on record; refused at construction for an API-key login, no login and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; an ask turn's argv (`exec --json --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check`, the two `-c` overrides, `-s read-only`, `-`), a 190 KB prompt on stdin, the profile 0600 with the key, the key on neither argv nor environment, the profile file gone and `$CODEX_HOME` empty afterwards, no billing variable in the child; an author turn's `workspace-write`, `-C`, the network override and the user's server turned off; a user server named `app` refused; timeout, exit-without-result and `turn.failed` each not measured; `--model` / `--author-model` / `--ask-model` → `-m`; both turn-cap flags refused.

<details><summary>Ablations (each restored: blob == HEAD, git diff HEAD empty)</summary>

Both through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor x1 → x0, replacement x0 → x1) on commit `fb1d76f7`. The suites import `src/` directly, so no dist leg.

- **Ablation 1, the key written into the record** (`external.ts` `ask`: `return await this.call(input, dir);` → the turn's `meta.model` set to `task.mcp.apiKey`): the end-to-end case → `1 failed | 7 skipped`, `expected [ …(7) ] to deeply equal []`, naming the run record, `recording.json`, `scorecard.md`, and the gallery's `README.md`, `run-record.json`, `scorecard.json`, `scorecard.md`.
- **Ablation 2, an API-key Codex login accepted** (`codex.ts`: the ChatGPT test widened to `/Logged in using ChatGPT|API key configured/`): `codex-driver.test.ts -t "cost guard|refuses an API-key login"` → `2 failed | 2 passed`, both "expected function to throw an error, but it didn't".
- Restore leg: both files → `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 20 passed (20)`.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **The external driver's cost claim.** `DriverInfo.apiBilled` is typed `false`, and the runner cannot see an external command's login, so the record says `authMethod: not verified (…)` and the README states the cost ruling applies to the command; the four billing variables are stripped from its environment. Whether an external command must also be refused when one of them is set in the caller's environment (as the two built-in drivers are) was not in the rulings; this PR strips and does not refuse.
- **No served model for Codex.** The JSONL names none, so a Codex turn's `model` is absent and the scorecard reads `model not reported (asked for …)` rather than guessing; `modelMismatch` is never set for it.
- **Codex writes into `$CODEX_HOME`.** The profile layer is the only key-in-a-file route the CLI was measured to read (`-p`); the file is 0600, uniquely named, and removed in `finally`. A run killed by SIGKILL could leave one behind; it holds a persona key of a local dev app that is torn down with the run.
- **The external stand-in's e2e uses the fixture's in-memory app.** The command answers the turn the scripted model gave; the double applies the turn's writes to the in-memory app in-process. Every turn's bytes still cross the process boundary, and the key reaches the command only through the file.
- `codex mcp list --json` prints the user's other servers' headers to the runner's memory once at start; only `name` is read and nothing is logged.
- Out of scope, untouched: any live model run (paused, cloud#3600), a WorkBuddy or other UI bridge, `orchestrate.ts`, the gallery `index.json` schema (the driver is on the app page, as Ask 4 says; `run-record.json` already carries `env.driver`).
